# LangChain Community migration

Inventory checked 2026-09-10 against #15019 (`db58ee8aa8`). This follow-up is stacked on
`fix/release-1.12.2-ml-cves` so the smaller security patch can ship independently.

**This batch reduces dependency edges; it does not remove `langchain-community` or
close its advisory.** Upstream [sunset the package](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-community/issues/674).
The replacements below use maintained provider packages, Core interfaces, or the
SDK surface the component actually needs. Component class names and input/output
identifiers stay unchanged.

## First batch

- Fake Embeddings uses `langchain_core.embeddings.FakeEmbeddings`.
- Oracle uses its provider's `DistanceStrategy`; floor `langchain-oracledb` at 1.5.0,
  where that export and independence from Community are verified.
- Db2 owns its distance enum and small NumPy MMR helper. It accepts legacy string
  enum values and preserves zero-vector/tie behavior (Core's private MMR helper
  rejects some all-zero inputs). Ingestion still strips all metadata and deduplicates
  document content. Database tables and stored data do not change.
- Chroma filters scalar metadata directly, retaining strings, booleans, integers,
  and floats. Containers and `None` are removed. Both embedded starter-flow copies
  are refreshed. Chroma itself, its advisories, and knowledge-base storage are unchanged.
- Apify fetches clean dataset items with its existing authenticated client and keeps
  field projection, nested-key flattening, logs, and completion waiting.
- Needle uses `needle.v1.NeedleClient`, preserving minimum-20 retrieval, tool query
  parsing, result formatting, empty metadata, and empty/error responses.
- Cloudflare uses `langchain-cloudflare~=0.3.9`, explicitly disabling the newly
  implicit `AI_GATEWAY` routing default. An executor adapter preserves the old async
  timeout behavior for slow successful responses. The provider validates empty credentials
  earlier and raises HTTP errors instead of parsing an error body as embeddings.
- Cohere 0.6 and Google Community 5 drop their hard Community requirements. Google
  Drive retains our single-Google-Doc path and supplied OAuth credentials; it avoids
  the new MIME-discovery `files.list` query, whose `id` term is absent from Google's
  [supported query terms](https://developers.google.com/workspace/drive/api/guides/ref-search-terms).

Couchbase is deferred from this candidate: `langchain-couchbase==1.1.1` starts Reo
telemetry on import. Suppressing it requires a process-wide deployment default; the
component environment-write guard requires resolving that configuration outside flow execution. Its SearchVectorStore
preserves the existing index/field layout in offline checks, but this side effect
needs resolution before adopting the package. Eight of the nine candidates ship here.

The lock retains LangChain 1.3.14, Core 1.5.1 and LangGraph 1.2.9. Version changes
are limited to Cohere/Google and the affected Langflow bundles. Cloudflare introduces
`sqlalchemy-cloudflare-d1`; deferred Couchbase would also add `reo-census`. New package
inventory must receive the same security scan as existing dependencies.

## Remaining work and release planning

The original inventory contains **50 direct-import Python files: 46 active and four
deactivated**. Nine first-batch candidates, 14 small adapters, 13 behavior adapters,
and 10 larger/product decisions partition the active files. The table below records
**every original import site**, including completed work, to keep removal scope auditable.
Paths are repository-relative; long-tail paths are under
`src/bundles/lfx-bundles/src/lfx_bundles/`.

Estimates are planning ranges, not measured delivery time. Shared adapters overlap;
do not add each file's range mechanically. The next small-adapter batch is roughly
2–4 engineer-days. Storage/agent migrations merit a separate release, such as 1.13,
unless particular integrations are deliberately retired or made manual opt-in.

### Indirect and dynamic routes

- `langchain-experimental==0.4.2` still requires Community and is also
  [sunset](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain-experimental/issues/87).
  Replace both Python REPL consumers, CSV agent, and SemanticChunker while preserving
  sandbox execution gates and chunking behavior.
- `agent-lifecycle-toolkit==0.12.0` and renamed `altk-boost==0.10.2` both retain
  Community. Request an upstream dependency split or make a separate retirement/manual
  opt-in decision. A declared optional extra still appears in the full Mend scan.
- `SelfQueryRetriever.from_llm` implicitly imports Community in Classic's automatic
  translator selection, even for dedicated stores. Supply explicit Community-free
  translators in `src/lfx/src/lfx/components/langchain_utilities/self_query.py`.
- `LANGFLOW_LANGCHAIN_CACHE` dynamically selects classes in
  `src/lfx/src/lfx/interface/utils.py`; define a supported replacement map.
- `LOADERS_INFO` contains 16 legacy loader names, with no discovered runtime consumer
  beyond its compatibility re-export. Remove or empty that unused registry deliberately;
  it does not require rebuilding 16 loaders.
- Classic's `SQLDatabase` alias forwards to Community. SQLGenerator also needs
  `.dialect` and `.get_table_info(table_names=...)` from any replacement SQL adapter.
- Refresh remaining generated component definitions, SaaS Pricing's embedded SQL
  component, and deprecated-import guidance as each consumer migrates. Keep historical
  saved-flow fixtures as compatibility evidence rather than bulk-rewriting them.

## Verification and full-removal gate

Successful local verification includes provider/adapter regressions, LFX dynamic-loading and
component-index suites, metadata and aggregate-extra tests; fresh-process migrated
imports with Community blocked; five affected bundle wheel builds; release metadata;
and exact generated index/starter source checks. The full workspace export compiles
for Python 3.12/Linux x86_64 with the CPU index, and the GP scope compiles against it.
The installed Community package is intentionally still present for deferred consumers.

Run provider contract tests plus local Chroma persistence, fresh-process imports with
Community blocked, bundle release-plan checks, metadata/lock checks, generated-source
checks, and wheel builds. Offline tests do not establish live provider-service behavior
or certify compatibility with every persisted database/index. Validate those integrations
with credentials before release.

Use the unchanged all-packages/all-extras/all-groups export and Python 3.12/Linux x86_64
CPU-index compile from [the Mend workflow](workflows/mend.yml). Include the GP script and
frontend scopes. **The workflow currently triggers only for PRs targeting `release-*` or
`main`; this stacked PR's `fix/...` base does not trigger it.** Run Mend after retargeting
onto the release branch, or through an approved exact-head workflow mechanism; do not
report a parent PR's run as validation of this migration.

Full removal requires deleting all remaining declared edges, including indirect consumers,
removing dynamic/implicit imports, and verifying that wheel requirements, lock, and full
export contain no Community. Test saved flows and existing stores, or provide an explicit
migration/rebuild path. A successful scanner execution is not advisory closure;
security-approved non-impact evidence or demonstrated remediation remains necessary.
